title: Degree distributions in the doctoral-advisor network
summary: People linked by who supervised whose doctorate (Wikidata P184). How many links each person has (degree) is heavy-tailed for advisors and thin-tailed for students; telling a power law from other heavy tails takes maximum likelihood, not a log-log line.

concepts.label: Academic genealogy network
concepts.description: A directed graph: an edge from advisor to student for each P184 statement.

facts.text: Wikidata property P184 (doctoral advisor) links a person to the person who supervised their doctorate.

children.label: Doctoral advisor
children.description: A person with at least one recorded student.

children.label: Students per advisor (out-degree)
children.description: k for advisors: heavy-tailed, mean 3.46, maximum 149.

children.label: Doctoral student
children.description: A person with at least one recorded advisor.

children.label: Advisors per student (in-degree)
children.description: k for students: thin-tailed, 81% have one, at most 12.

children.label: Field of work
children.description: The advisor's discipline (P101): tails may differ between mathematics and the lab sciences.

children.label: Doctoral year
children.description: When each supervision ended: needed to watch the network grow.

concepts.label: Heavy-tailed distribution
concepts.description: A distribution whose tail falls slower than any exponential: rare values are far more common than a thin-tailed model of the same mean predicts.

children.label: Power law
children.description: P(K ≥ k) ∝ k^(1−α) above x_min; a straight line on log-log axes.

facts.text: Clauset, Shalizi & Newman (2009) showed that many claimed power laws fail a maximum-likelihood fit with a KS-chosen x_min and a likelihood-ratio test.

children.label: Maximum-likelihood exponent
children.description: α = 1 + n / Σ ln(k/(x_min − ½)), with standard error (α − 1)/√n.

children.label: KS distance
children.description: Largest gap between empirical and fitted CCDF; minimised to choose x_min.

children.label: Likelihood-ratio test (Vuong)
children.description: Power law against an alternative: R, z, p and a verdict.

children.label: Lognormal and power law with cutoff
children.description: Alternatives that also bend on log-log axes; not fitted here.

concepts.label: Cumulative advantage
concepts.description: Preferential attachment (Price 1976, Barabási–Albert 1999): nodes with many links gain new ones faster, giving heavy tails; the Matthew effect in science (Merton 1968).

facts.text: Merton named the Matthew effect in science in 1968: eminent scientists get disproportionate credit.

concepts.label: Wikidata coverage
concepts.description: Which supervisions editors have entered: bulk imports and famous names over-represented; a source bias in the tail.
